reason: The introduction says to line the wooden binding boards with paper, so I'll place the planks at the library table.
expectation: I expect the planks to be ready for combining with paper at the table, though I don't yet know the exact result.

alternatives.reason: Paper also belongs in the lining step, but I chose to place the boards first.

effect: The planks are at the library table, and paper can now be combined with them there.
reason: The introduction says to line the binding boards with paper, so this directly advances that task.
expectation: I expect paper-lined binding boards, ready to receive the studies.

effect: The lined binding boards have four named slots, so I can add the studies in any order.
reaction: The result matches the expected next step.
reason: I'll add the botanical sheets to fill the plants slot.
expectation: I expect the botanical sheets to be fitted into the boards, leaving the other three slots open.

effect: The botanical sheets are fitted, leaving the other three studies to add.
reason: I'll add the pond drawings to fill another study slot.
expectation: I expect the pond drawings to be fitted alongside the botanical sheets.

effect: The pond drawings are fitted; the weather record and star chart remain.
reason: I'll add the weather record to fill the next study slot.
expectation: I expect the weather record to be fitted alongside the other studies, leaving the stars slot open.

effect: The weather record is fitted, leaving the star chart to complete the four studies.
reason: The star chart is the only remaining study and the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the star chart to fill the last slot and complete the gathering goal.

effect: The star chart completed the four studies, and the binding goal is now available.
reason: Thread is the only offered combination and should bind the gathered studies.
expectation: I expect the thread to stitch the boards and studies into an encyclopedia.

effect: The thread bound the gathered studies into an encyclopedia and completed the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate studies become a usable reference.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding the encyclopedia brought the four studies together into a volume with a clear purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the four studies one at a time became repetitive, since each worked as expected.

surprise.text: The boards revealed named slots for each study, making the remaining assembly clear.

arbitrary.text: None felt especially arbitrary; the introduction explained the assembly, though the order of the studies was a matter of choice.

continue.text: I probably would not continue immediately: the final volume was satisfying, but the repeated fittings offered few meaningful decisions.
